## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

Let me think carefully about scene design for beauty.

**World**
- Coordinate: Y up, world ~ radius 600 units. Terrain: procedural heightfield 1200x1200 plane segmented 256, height via layered fbm with valley around origin, mountains at distance, ocean plane at y=-20 maybe. Player starts above a green valley. Water bay to the west. Cliffs.
- Sky: custom shader dome with gradient from warm horizon to blue zenith, sun disc glow, wispy cloud band, subtle dithering. Perhaps use sky shader then fog warm.
- Sun: directional light from low-ish golden angle, shadows.
- Clouds: procedural cumulus made of instanced spheres with toon material + fresnel; placed at y 80-160. To look Ghibli, add "cloud sea" layer far below? Actually top-down clouds at horizon. A big cumulus around floating islands.
- Mountains: distant cone/ridges with blue-ish atmospheric tint, placed around. Use custom geometry ridges.
- Floating islands? Adds fantasy Ghibli. A few floating islands with grass top, rock underside, trees, waterfall. Great visual identity. But physics can just ignore (no collision needed, or collide gentle). Implement 2 floating islands with small trees.
- Village: tiny Ghibli windmill on a hill with red roof and white walls, windmill blades rotating. Maybe a house cluster near start. Distant tower. Adds charm.
- Ocean with stylized waves shader: gradient turquoise, sun glitter, foam lines via noise? Could use MeshStandardMaterial with custom onBeforeCompile or ShaderMaterial. A cheap beautiful approach: custom ShaderMaterial with gerstner-ish waves displacing vertices, color based on normal & fresnel, plus sparkle. Add white foam rings near shore? Terrain defines coast. Simpler: a large plane at y=0 with shallow gradient and waves; terrain rising above water. Use shader.
- Grass: instanced blades near player, thousands, sway shader. But from bird altitude, grass not visible much. Add instanced flowers? Perhaps not performance-critical; use color variation in terrain plus clumps of trees.
- Trees: ~250 low-poly stylized trees: trunk + 3-5 foliage blobs with flat-shaded toon material, varied greens. Instanced? Since unique positioning can use merged geometry or individual meshes sharing geometry/material, still fine (250*5). Use InstancedMesh for foliage spheres and trunks for perf. But variety in color via instance colors. Trees bulge silhouettes; use dodecahedron geometry with noise? Ghibli trees: rounded canopy clusters. Icosahedron geometry detail 1, scale non-uniform, flatShading toon. Good.
- Birds flock in distance (animated V formation) adds life.
- Particles: floating pollen/spirit motes near player, golden. Also wind streak lines when diving.
- Ring gates: glowing torii-like rings? Ghibli-esque "wind gates" as rings of pale gold light with little paper streamers. Use torus + shader glow + particles. Add 12 collectible spirits in a course.
- Great Tree at center/hill, huge, as hub; when all collected it blooms (spawns pink blossoms + light beam/fireworks).

**Lighting & post**
- ACES tone mapping? For anime palette, use custom color grade. Use ACESFilmic with exposure 1.1.
- Bloom for sun/spirits (UnrealBloomPass strength ~0.5, radius .6, threshold .9).
- Vignette + slight chromatic aberration? Use custom ShaderPass color grade (lift shadows warm, teal in shadows, soft contrast); plus FXAA. Maybe use output pass.
- Ghibli painterly: fog warm blue, sun rays via radial gradient sky shader; maybe god rays post not needed.
- Film grain subtle.

**Bird**
We need appealing model. Build group:
- body: elongated ellipsoid white, head sphere, beak orange cone, eyes black with white highlight.
- wings: each wing is a group at shoulder, built from several feather planes (extruded boxes? thin tapered shapes). Could generate custom feather geometry: shape with rounded tip, use DoubleSide toon material with slight gradient. 6 primary feathers per wing + covert layer. Wing shape: swept. Animate flap rotation Z axis and feather spread. Also wingtip fingers bend.
- tail: fan of 5 feathers.
- Feet tucked.
- Animation: glide with slight wing curve, flap cycle 1.2s, tip feathers lag. Banking: roll based on horizontal turn, pitch based on vertical speed. Body yaw follows velocity. Use smooth quaternion.
- Maybe camera offset.

Bird scale relative to world: bird ~2.5 units long; camera 8 units behind. Terrain features human scale.

**Flight physics**
Arcade glide: forward speed base 26, boost dive up to 60, flap gives speed/up impulse and costs stamina. Gravity pulls and lift proportional to speed, with pitch controlling climb/dive. Controls:
- W/S or Up/Down: pitch (nose down/up). Actually flight convention: W = dive, S = climb. Mouse? Let's use W/↑ dive, S/↓ climb, A/D or ←/→ turn (roll+turn), Space flap (boost), Shift tuck/dive. 
- Simpler fun: Bird auto-flies forward. A/D steer left/right (banked turn). W pitch down, S pitch up. Space flap (boost + slight climb). Shift = speed boost dive. 
- Camera follows with damping; mouse drag rotates view around for look, spring back? Add optional.
- Collision: terrain check; if too close, bounce? Soft crash with respawn at last safe point, screen flash. Ocean splash respawn. Keep forgiving.
- Stamina (wind): flap consumes; regen while gliding/diving. Orbs restore.

**Objectives**
- 10 "Wind Spirits" (soft glowing orbs with trails) at positions along a scenic route: over lake, through stone arch, near waterfall, above forest canopy, around floating island, inside cloud. Each collect requires proximity. A compass/marker points to nearest.
- 5 "sky rings" maybe combined: flying through rings gives boost & points. Could be too much. Let's do spirits only + rings marking route? The spirits are enough with a mini-map. Actually rings are satisfying; combine: 8 rings, each ring contains a spirit at center; flying through collects. That's clear objective: "Fly through the wind gates" (8 gates). Each ring gives time? HUD shows count and nearest direction arrow + distance. Free flight continues after. Timer counts up; best time stored. Additionally collectible "pollen" small orbs for score? Keep focus.

Better: sky now blue-ish gray at top. Still muddy yellow-green overall, but more atmospheric. The bird now visible with dark tail/wingtips? Wings still thin white sticks. There is a huge gate glow at bottom center (nearest) and one at right mid (another gate) which looks like a sun. The floating island right is a dark UFO. The great tree is green and centered; nice but not majestic. The lake at bottom is turquoise but mostly hidden by card. Hmm.

Major issues:
1. Title card covers 60% of screen, and the composition's best parts (lake) are behind. Menu card too wide/tall. Could reduce width to 28rem and make background slightly more transparent, moving focus. Also position card higher/lower? The card is fine but covers the view.
2. The world still looks muddy because of the **warm yellow-green overlay**. The sky has a blue-gray tint with yellow haze. The image appears desaturated and low contrast. Ghibli palette is saturated greens, blue sky, white clouds. We need to push saturation and contrast significantly. Perhaps our post **film grain and vignette** are muddying. But the dominant issue could be the great amount of fog/haze and the sun glow. Also the toon gradient for trees has shadow steps that are dark desaturated. The terrain texture multiply (#cfd4b8) dulls colors. Let's remove/lighten texture tint and boost saturation.

Let's compare pixel colors: sky top #8897a0-ish gray-blue; expected #4a8fce. Because of the horizon mix? At h maybe 0.15 t=0.51, mix(horizon cream, zenith blue) → gray-lavender. To get blue at the top of the frame, use t=pow(h, 0.24) and/or make horizon color more blue. At h=0.15, t=.63; mix of #f7d6a3 and #2f6fae → still grayish. The top of the menu screenshot is maybe 10° above horizon (h=.17), so with pow .34 t=.55. Ghibli scenes would still be light blue at 10°, not gray. The warm horizon haze band could be narrower. Set horizon color a light blue #cfe1e6 and add warm only near horizon (0.03) with uHaze. Then at h=.17 t=.55 mix light blue #cfe1e6 with zenith blue #2f6fae → medium blue. Yes! The current uHorizon is cream, causing the gray-yellow. Use `uHorizon = #cfe2e8` (pale cyan) and `uHaze = #f0d9b0` applied only below h<0.08. Then sky is blue above with warm band at horizon. This should transform the image.
Also fog color maybe pale blue #ccdcde. Distant mountains then blue-gray, nice.

3. **Sun direction** means the scene's light is warm but sun is behind camera-left; the background sky opposite sun should be blue. Good.
4. **Water** turquoise shows at bottom but the bright gate light blows out. Once gate material is tone-mapped, it's a soft yellow orb (still big). Could reduce.

5. **Clouds** are now giant and look like floating blobs. The one at right is huge and close because maybe at (250,262,-70) 600m? It appears as a big white cloud at top-right, but its bottom is cut by island. It looks okay-ish, though the puffs form a solid mass with flat shading. The cloud at center-left is small. Need softer edges; sprite halo might help. But clouds are acceptable for stylized. We can make their shading more blue in shadows (emissive) and add a little variation. Later.

6. **Floating island** right is a dark striped cone (UFO), bad. The cone geometry shows black triangle facets and the rock is too dark. Improve with:
   - lighter rock color #8d8271, emissive slight.
   - less regular cone: already displaced but still triangular facets. Add more radial segments (18) and height segments, flatShading true. Dark shadows because sun from behind? The island is at (386,240,-96), sun from northwest, so its underside is shadowed; from camera it's backlit, looking black. Add a fill light or emissive to rock. Or reposition islands so they're sunlit. Sun direction (-0.48,0.42,-0.72) from northwest; camera faces east. The right island is southeast of camera? Its underside faces camera → dark. Use a brighter material and `emissive: #3a342c intensity .35`, plus hemisphere light. Could help. Also add moss/vines bright green. But overall floating islands may look like UFOs. Maybe remove islands near the menu view and place them far as background. Move right island to (520, 260, -420) so it's far and small. Left island maybe at (-520,260,-420). Both north. Since camera faces east, they'd be at left edge/horizon. This declutters the view. But they are a nice fantasy landmark. Could place one directly in the middle distance to the **north** so it's not in this view; exploration finds it. I think remove from the opening composition. Set islands at (-520, 260, -480) and (600, 280, -380). They'll be distant.
   - Their dark undersides still show when encountered. Improve material.
7. **Great Tree** trunk appears gray/pale due to fog? At 400m fog minimal; bark material #6b513b lit by sun should be brown. It appears gray-brown, okay. Canopy green. Could add a warmer light at the top? no.
8. **The gate at bottom center** (nearest) is very bright and sits under the title card, ugly. Move gate 3 up/away slightly? The first gate is at (-292, 82, 96) below bird (138). It's 106m ahead and 56m below → screen bottom. That's okay in gameplay but in menu it's under card. Shift gate 3 to (-292, 118, 96) (higher) so it's mid-screen, and maybe to the right? Its x position right of center? From bird yaw -0.92, gate direction yaw -0.825 (slightly left/right?). desiredYaw -0.825 > bird yaw -0.92 means target is to the left? relative = +0.095 => left. Screen x slightly left. Under card. Could move gate 3 to (-250, 120, 20) so more to the right? From start, dx=120,dz=-148, yaw=atan2(-120,148)=-0.68 (to the right of heading -0.92) → screen right. But then it's over land/shore. Let's reposition the course start: gate 3 "A Drift of Pollen" at (-250, 120, 30) (near the lake's eastern shore, above land height maybe 30). Then it's 190m ahead-right, screen right. Menu shows it glowing in the valley rather than under card. Great.
   - But gate 2 (-158,82,8) then gate 3 etc. Loop still works. Nearest gate from start: gate3 distance sqrt(120²+148²+18²)=194; gate2 distance sqrt(212²+160²+56²)=271; gate4 309. So gate3 nearest. Fine.
9. **Bird**: Looks better but wings are thin and pointy like an airplane. Need more bird-like wing shape. We can widen the feather fan and add layered coverts:
   - The wing viewed from above should have a broad inner wing and fingered primaries. Currently feathers all root along the arm and extend as narrow blades, yielding thin sticks. The screenshot shows two thin white lines, because the camera is almost exactly behind and the wings are edge-on? No, if horizontal, from slightly above we should see surfaces. The camera is 2.1 above bird looking slightly up? Camera above bird by 2.1, so sees wing tops at a shallow angle; the wings appear as thin lines because they're nearly edge-on. In a 3rd-person bird game, you want to see the wings; camera should be higher (5-7 above) and look down at the bird, or the bird should be banked. Our earlier camera height 3.5 showed flat white wings. Let's set gameplay/menu camera higher and offset down look? For menu, camera 4.5 above bird (looking slightly down) would show wing surfaces and the valley. The screenshot with height 3.5 showed big wings but visible. We reduced height to 2.1 to get more sky; that's why wings are edge-on. Compromise: height 3.6, look target 2.6 above bird, so view slightly down but still sky. Or bank the bird in menu with a slight roll (0.12) to show one wing. Better: menu camera height 4.0, look target 2.0 above, giving medium downward view and more sky than before? The camera above by 4.0, target 2.0 above → down angle 2/16 = 7°, horizon ~top third. Wings visible. Add slight bank in idle (visual only) 0.07. This also shows bird's back. Good.
   - For gameplay, camera height 3.2 above, look target 1.35 above → 8° down, wing visible at shallow angle. Maybe okay.
10. **Bird body** currently a white oval with a pointy tail; head and beak hard to see; we can tilt the bird slightly in menu so its profile is visible. Bank 0.08.

11. **Landscape vegetation** is repetitive lollipop trees with sparse coverage. Could add denser forest clusters on hills, larger tree canopies, and **grass/meadow detail**. From the air, the meadow looks like plain textured green. Adding patches of flowers (Points) might show as colored specks; current flowers exist but perhaps too small/sparse. Increase flower count and size? Points size 1.15 might be tiny. Add wildflower patches via vertex color patches (blossom tint) — we did subtle. Could add **clusters of colored trees** (sakura) and **rock outcrops** near grass. And a **river** or streams. Let's consider a river: a winding blue ribbon across the meadow would add major beauty. The terrain height function doesn't include a river; we could overlay a low-elevation water mesh shaped by a path. A river running from the lake east across the valley at elevation? The lake is at sea level y=2; a river would need to be at descending elevation, complex. Instead add a **highland pond** in the valley with its own water plane. Hmm.

We could also build **terraced fields** near the village (Ghibli touch): small patchwork green rectangles on hillsides. At aerial view these read as agriculture. Add a few rectangular patches of lighter/darker green on terrain? Could place flat planes slightly above ground with different green colors following slope; might z-fight. Better use vertex colors in terrain: add large rectangular patches rotated? Hard in heightfield colors but doable: define farm regions (center, size, rotation) and tint within. Also add field boundaries. This could enrich the valley. But might look odd.
   - Maybe add **stone walls** and **haystacks**? Not needed.

12. **Distant mountains** lack snow/rock detail. Increase height and snow. At the horizon they are pale blue silhouettes, good.
13. **Sky birds flock** visible (tiny line) adds life. Good.
14. **Pollen particles** are prominent white dots everywhere; could reduce size/opacity slightly. They look like snow. In Ghibli, floating pollen is nice, but 720 dots is a lot. Reduce opacity .55, size .55, count 500. Also the white dots on dark card look like stars. Keep some.
15. **UI** top left objective box has a big blank area (padding). It's fine but maybe reduce.
16. **Post grain** maybe makes it muddy. Keep.

Let's implement color/sky/cloud/island/camera/gate/bird changes. First sky horizon color and fog. Change uHorizon to #bcd8e4 or #cfe4ec. uHaze to #f6d9ac. Fog color #cfdfe2. This gives blue sky.
Also `uHaze` applies smoothstep(0.11,...)*0.82 near horizon; with cream still a warm band. Good.

Change terrain grass texture tint: base fill '#cfd4b8' maybe to '#d9ddc4' (brighter) and reduce stroke opacity. This will make colors brighter. Also `map` is multiplied; near white is better. Set base '#dde0c9'. Fine.

Post saturation 1.12, contrast 1.05, vignette lighter 0.8. Maybe no.

Sun light warmth and intensity. With NeutralToneMapping, colors should be more saturated. We'll see.

Camera menu height 3.8 look +2.3; this frames bird and wing surfaces. Actually to keep sky, look target 2.8? Let's set camera height 3.7, look target +2.2, distance 16.2 → down angle (3.7-2.2)/16=5.3°. Bird vertical angle relative: bird 3.7 below camera at 16 → 13° below horizontal; view center 5.3° down, so bird 7.7° below center → y=-0.17. Good. Horizon slightly above center. Wings visible better. Add idle roll 0.05.

Gameplay camera height 4.2, look target +1.5 → down 9.6°; bird below camera 4.2 at 12.6 → 18.4° below horizontal, relative center -8.8° → y -0.19. Fine. Wings visible. Let's set gameplay height 4.0, distance 12.8. Bird appears lower but good.

Gate 3 reposition. Gate materials. Floating islands. Clouds maybe later.

Bird wing shape: make feathers wider and more overlapping so wing reads as a surface:
- width `0.32 + (1-t)*0.25` (currently .24+.2).
- lengths 1.7 + t*2.7.
- rotation.y = -0.09 - (1-t)*0.5.
- Add an inner secondary feather layer at z +0.25, shorter, to fill the wing. Or a wing membrane mesh under the feathers with cream color. Could add a broad flat wing shape (like a rounded triangle) under the feather fan to fill gaps, semi-white. Construct `ShapeGeometry` with a wing planform, position at shoulder, material cream double side. This will give a solid wing and the feathers on top for detail. The wing membrane can be built using a Shape with points:
```
shape.moveTo(0,0.6) // leading root
bezier to (3.7,0.2) tip
line to (3.2,-0.6) trailing
bezier back to (0.2,-1.1)
```

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D bird flight game with realistic, anime-stylized Ghibli-inspired graphics, flying anywhere above a painted valley.

## Requirements
- Single build request; do not ask clarifying questions; make assumptions and note them briefly at the end.
- Must be playable now, including desktop and mobile/touch support (repo guidance requires responsive layouts, usable touch controls, safe areas, no browser gesture conflicts).
- Visually high quality, realistic yet Ghibli/anime painterly.

## Decisions
- Vite + Three.js r0.169, fully procedural world/assets/audio (no external files).
- Third-person white gull/heron with arcade flight physics: banked turns, climb/dive energy trade, flapping, stamina/wind regen, forgiving crash respawn.
- Game goal: collect 9 glowing “wind spirit” gates; completing all awakens/b looms the Elder Tree and shows a completion card.
- Ghibli palette via custom sky/water/cloud/grade shaders, toon foliage, warm sun, blue sky, pink blossom trees, lake, mountains, Great Tree, floating islands, village/windmill, pollen, distant bird flock.
- Start relocated above the western lake at `(-370, 138, 168)`, yaw `-0.92`, facing the Elder Tree with water foreground.
- Menu renders live 3D scene with title card on left; HUD uses cream/sage serif style; touch joystick + FLAP/DIVE buttons.
- No audio files; procedural wind, wingbeats, chimes, sparse pentatonic score.
- Support `?autostart=1` and `?quality=low`; expose `window.__KAZE` debug handle.

## Work State
### Completed
- Vite project, all HTML/CSS/UI overlays (menu, HUD, pause, completion, touch controls), loading screen.
- Three.js world: procedural terrain, lake water shader, sky shader with cirrus, sun, lighting/shadows/fog, 620 instanced trees with blossom variants, flowers, village + windmill, Elder Tree + torii, 2 floating islands/waterfalls, 11 clouds, 9 gates with beacons/streamers/wisps, pollen, distant flock.
- Bird model and flight controls, camera follow, collisions/boundaries, gate collection, completion flow, best time persistence, procedural audio.
- First successful renders and two iterations of major visual fixes: fixed Bird constructor crash (`this.model` used before creation); blue sky via horizon color; higher cloud quality via custom cloud shader; more wings/feathers contrast; sun/bloom/gate beam reduced; moved start to lake; improved gate/tree/camera composition.
- Production build succeeds (`npm run build`); dev server runs on `http://localhost:3002` via tmux session `kaze`.

### Active
- Continuing visual polish after adding forest detail hook: just inserted `this._createForestDetails();` in `World` constructor, but the method itself is **not yet implemented** — game will currently throw during startup until added.
- Plan: add conifers/pines, boulders/shrubs; then re-test menu/gameplay screenshots.

### Blocked
- None, aside from the missing `_createForestDetails()` method which must be added immediately before next reload.

## Next Move
1. Implement `World._createForestDetails()` in `src/world.js` with InstancedMesh conifers (layered cones, dark green instance colors) and instanced boulders on slopes/meadows, avoiding water, village, elder-tree glade, and start clearing.
2. Run `npm run build`; reload Playwright with `DISPLAY=:0 playwright-cli reload` and capture menu/game.
3. Improve bird readability: widen wing chord (`wing.scale.z ≈ 1.3`) and slim body/lengthen neck; verify wings visible from chase camera.
4. Possibly add field/patchwork tints, stronger flower meadow colors, better Great Tree shape, reduce intro toast dominance, tune saturation/lighting.
5. Verify gameplay: keyboard flight, gate collection, pause/resume, restart, completion overlay, mobile viewport/touch controls, no console errors.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: procedural terrain, water, sky, trees, clouds, village, Elder Tree, islands, gates, pollen; missing `_createForestDetails()`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: renderer/composer/post grade, game state, camera, HUD wiring, input, collisions, completion.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/bird.js`: bird model, wing/feather materials, flight physics, idle animation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/styles.css`: title menu, HUD, touch controls, responsive/safe-area rules.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: all UI markup and SVG assets.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: procedural Web Audio soundscape.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/textures.js`: canvas textures/toon gradients/glow/dot/petal/grass/cloud.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/effects.js`: spark burst effects.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/utils.js`: noise/fbm/math helpers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: scripts/deps (`npm run dev`, `npm run build`).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: captured menu/game iterations, latest `menu7.png`, `game3.png`.

## Important Context
- Latest screenshots: `screenshots/menu7.png` (blue sky, soft clouds, lake, bird, title card) and `screenshots/game3.png` (gameplay HUD, lake, valley, Elder Tree, intro toast).
- Dev server: tmux session `kaze`, `npm run dev`, port 3002.
- Playwright requires `DISPLAY=:0`; browser installed via `playwright-cli install-browser chromium`; viewport currently 1050×793.

- Known remaining issues: wings still read thin/edge-on; bird body looks somewhat duck-like; valley vegetation still somewhat sparse/repetitive; floating islands can read as dark UFOs; intro toast large; no implemented `_createForestDetails()` yet.
- All work is uncommitted; git repo has unrelated initial tracked setup commit and untracked scaffold files.
